notes_for_editor: The only source for this tower is one row of the tnlandforms GA list (GA290, coordinates, elevation, GFC 119, BLL-64694, which carries a 'usgs' tag). No NHLR, FFLOS, Vanishing Georgia or Wikimedia Commons page in our caches names it, and two web searches turned up no lookout history, only fire-station and town pages. The list's naming note applies because GA290 is above 73, so 'Ellabell' is a label. The list gives elevations with no unit on the page, so the story now gives 79 with no unit. The tower record (data/towers/ga/us-ga-ellabell.json) reads it as feet and has elevation_m 24.1; that conversion is not in any source and needs the editor's decision. Status, build date, design, staffing and access are all unknown. The GFC contact page is cited only for the Bryan North unit's address, which describes the county unit, not this tower. The story no longer says that unit is the place to ask about access, because the source gives only its address. The 2006 Savannah Morning News article on Georgia fire towers (see the Elberton notes) names no Bryan County tower in the text we read. Story is about 150 words. Verification 2026-10-21: one unsourced unit fixed, one unsupported access claim removed, one near-verbatim phrase reworded; all 5 quotes found on the first check.
